transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Um... well, my supervisor told me I had to come. I guess... I keep leaving my station on the floor. And sometimes during our shift meetings, I just kind of... pop up when I'm supposed to be sitting. They said it's turning into a safety issue, because I just... take off before I even realize I'm doing it.
Have you been getting into fights or physical arguments with other people?
No... I don't get into fights with anybody.
Do you often have trouble paying attention when you need to focus?

Yeah, I guess. Um... like if I have to do the inventory logs, or... read the CNC training pages. I start out trying, but... after a few minutes, the numbers and words just kind of blur together. I have to keep going back over it because I didn't really... take any of it in.
Before age 12, did you already have similar trouble paying attention or sitting still?

Yeah... I guess so. Um... even back in elementary school, I was kind of that kid. I couldn't really stay in my seat. I got a lot of notes sent home because I'd... talk over the teacher, or blurt things out. Or just end up wandering around the room.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive/combined presentation, with clear childhood onset and current impairment. He reports difficulty sustaining attention, repeatedly leaving his station and rising when expected to stay seated, blurting/talking over the teacher in childhood, and wandering around the room before age 12. Symptoms are causing functional and safety problems at work. No evidence was given for a conduct disorder or another better explanation.
